No bug: the change is a pure refactor. np.linalg.norm(c_i - c_j, axis=1) equals sqrt(sum of squared differences), and the boundary and radius constraints are the same, in the same order. The packing is still validated by the harness, so the result stays meaningful.

Because the code does the same thing, no real gain is expected. The observed 2.6261 vs 2.6280 (0.0019 worse in loss) is within the noise of one run (sd 0.0023). It makes the code a bit longer for no benefit, so rejecting it is reasonable.

Recomputed z: (incumbent loss - candidate loss) / (0.0023 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/10)) = (-2.6280 + 2.6261) / 0.002412 ≈ -0.79. This matches the harness value of -0.793 up to rounding of the reported means. With only one candidate run, the evidence is weak either way, and the provisional reject agrees with the numbers.
